title: Hourly urine output trend in acute kidney injury
scenario: A 58-year-old client is being monitored after developing acute kidney injury following sepsis. The nurse tracks hourly urine output from the indwelling catheter.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the urine output trend over the past four hours?

options.text: Urine output is progressively declining into oliguria and indicates worsening kidney injury
Urine output is within normal limits and requires no action
Urine output is improving and the catheter can be removed
The falling output reflects normal overnight variation

questions.rationale: Output has fallen from 42 to 10 mL/hr, well below the 0.5 mL/kg/hr (about 35 mL/hr) threshold, meeting the definition of oliguria and signalling worsening acute kidney injury.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the trend, what is the nurse's most appropriate next action?

options.text: Notify the provider of the declining urine output and falling MAP
Document the trend and reassess at the end of the shift
Encourage the client to increase oral fluids independently
Irrigate the catheter and take no further action

questions.rationale: Oliguria with a falling mean arterial pressure signals deterioration that exceeds independent nursing measures, so the nurse must promptly notify the provider for further orders. Delayed reassessment or routine measures would leave the deterioration untreated.
